svg.text: Cartridge end caps — every Keystone contact in place
Cartridge end caps — every Keystone contact in place
Both caps drawn AS SEEN FROM OUTSIDE — the face the links run on. That mirrors the base cap in X relative to the top cap; the cell labels are the authority, not the corner.

Both caps are the SAME printed part (0.9-deep INBOARD pockets, a wire slot under each plate), the top cap it flipped about X. Plates, springs, buttons: far side, drawn through.

Read the cell labels, not the corners — the two views are mirrored.

The base cap is drawn from BELOW because that is the face its links are soldered on, so its X axis is flipped against the top view. C1 is upper-LEFT on the top cap and upper-RIGHT on the base cap.
The base cap is drawn from BELOW because that is the face its links are soldered on, so its X axis is flipped against the top view. C1 is upper-LEFT on the top cap and upper-RIGHT on the base cap.
It is the same cell in both. Getting this backwards swaps link A with link C and puts the balance taps on the wrong cells — a BMS fault, not a dead short, so it will not announce itself.
It is the same cell in both. Getting this backwards swaps link A with link C and puts the balance taps on the wrong cells — a BMS fault, not a dead short, so it will not announce itself.
Every contact on one cap is the SAME part — the polarity labels do not choose it.
Every contact on one cap is the SAME part — the polarity labels do not choose it.

Keystone calls 5222 the “negative spring” and 5221 the “positive button”, which are conventions from AA alkalines with a raised + nub. Our 26700s are FLAT-TOP at both ends, so a flat cap meets whichever contact is there.

Keystone calls 5222 the “negative spring” and 5221 the “positive button”, which are conventions from AA alkalines with a raised + nub. Our 26700s are FLAT-TOP at both ends, so a flat cap meets whichever contact is there.

The spring/button split here is purely MECHANICAL: all four springs go on one cap because a spring is what takes up cell-length tolerance, and all four buttons on the other because the button is the rigid datum. Do not try to

match part names to the + and − marks on this drawing — the top cap carries a “negative spring” on C1, which is the pack POSITIVE terminal, and that is correct.
match part names to the + and − marks on this drawing — the top cap carries a “negative spring” on C1, which is the pack POSITIVE terminal, and that is correct.
Five nets leave the cartridge, and only two caps carry them.
Five nets leave the cartridge, and only two caps carry them.

TOP: pack+ at C1, pack− at C4, and tap B2 off link B. BASE: tap B1 off link A, tap B3 off link C. The rod is SOLID, so B1 and B3 leave the base cap through the Ø2.2 hole at r 25 on +X, run up the OUTSIDE

TOP: pack+ at C1, pack− at C4, and tap B2 off link B. BASE: tap B1 off link A, tap B3 off link C. The rod is SOLID, so B1 and B3 leave the base cap through the Ø2.2 hole at r 25 on +X, run up the OUTSIDE

of the pack in the valley between two cells (outside the spacer wall), pass the top cap through the same hole, and join the other three at the 5-pin JST-XH. Tap each link at its midpoint, not at a plate.

of the pack in the valley between two cells (outside the spacer wall), pass the top cap through the same hole, and join the other three at the 5-pin JST-XH. Tap each link at its midpoint, not at a plate.
The two taps are 26 AWG and pass the caps INSULATED (they run outside the pack), so the hole is sized for two jackets.
The two taps are 26 AWG and pass the caps INSULATED (they run outside the pack), so the hole is sized for two jackets.
BOTH caps: each link / pack lead comes up a 5 × 4 WIRE SLOT through the CENTRE of its pocket and is soldered to the BACK of the plate; the 18 AWG silicone (Ø3.3) insulation stops

in the slot mouth. Strain relief is done off the part (Soldering Guide §16.5). The links run slot centre to slot centre, all at r ≥ 13 — well outside the nut.
in the slot mouth. Strain relief is done off the part (Soldering Guide §16.5). The links run slot centre to slot centre, all at r ≥ 13 — well outside the nut.
Every plate is held by TWO M1.2 × 2.5 self-tappers, on BOTH caps.
Every plate is held by TWO M1.2 × 2.5 self-tappers, on BOTH caps.
The screws go through the plate’s OWN Ø1.40 / Ø1.57 holes (10.1 apart), so the plates are unmodified. Two, not one: the cell spring load is continuous and off-axis, and one screw lets the plate

pivot and peel. All eight pockets sit the same way round. Each cap also carries 4 Ø1 pilots at (±21.06, ±21.06) for the cell spacer’s M1.2 × 3 countersunk screws — the spacer screwed

to its cap is what holds the pack on the rod. Plate pockets 11.2 × 13.1, 0.9 deep — the 0.51 plate sits 0.39 below the rim.
to its cap is what holds the pack on the rod. Plate pockets 11.2 × 13.1, 0.9 deep — the 0.51 plate sits 0.39 below the rim.
On the top cap the spring presses its plate INTO the pocket, so the screws only locate; their heads sit beside the spring’s base coil (measured Ø7.25 vs head inner edge r 4.05 → 0.43 mm clear).
On the top cap the spring presses its plate INTO the pocket, so the screws only locate; their heads sit beside the spring’s base coil (measured Ø7.25 vs head inner edge r 4.05 → 0.43 mm clear).
The caps are FLAT — the M8 thread is a separate hex nut on the outboard face.
The caps are FLAT — the M8 thread is a separate hex nut on the outboard face.
Each cap is a 3.3 mm Ø66 disc with a plain Ø8.4 hole; a 13 AF × 7 M8 nut (one part, printed twice) screws onto the rod from outside and clamps it — the springs push the disc OUTWARD onto

its nut (compression). The caps print OUTBOARD FACE DOWN: flat bed face, pockets as clean top surfaces, no supports. 7 mm = 5.6 turns engaged in the nut.
its nut (compression). The caps print OUTBOARD FACE DOWN: flat bed face, pockets as clean top surfaces, no supports. 7 mm = 5.6 turns engaged in the nut.
⚠ Still open from the cartridge work: flat-top cells cannot be keyed against reversal.

Nothing on either cap stops a user seating a cell backwards — both ends are flat and both contacts will touch. That is a circuit-side problem, not a cap-geometry one, and it is unresolved.
